title: Tenant provenance and cohort-heuristic dashboard notes
content:
Purpose:
This is a working planning doc for a compact, cost-aware observability surface that ties session-level provenance into tenant/cohort dashboards. Goal: enable fast investigation flow for latency and correctness anomalies while bounding query and trace costs across tenants.

Design principles (short):
- Tenant-weighted signals: keep per-tenant cardinality low, but surface per-cohort anomalies.
- Session provenance first: store a single session_provenance_id on requests to stitch traces and reconstruct multi-call journeys.
- Cost-aware dashboards: panels show both signal and query-cost to help trade off alert sensitivity.
- Progressive rollout: instrument minimal core metrics first, then expand histograms and span annotations.

Key metric definitions (proposal):
1) inference.request.latency_ms (histogram)
   - description: end-to-end wall-clock latency for a single inference request (start = req received, end = final token emitted).
   - unit: ms
   - SLI: p50/p95/p99 per-cohort
   - cardinality tags: model, region, tenant_cohort (see cohort logic below)
   - rollup: store coarse quantiles in long-term metrics; full distribution for 7d only.

2) inference.kv_cache.warmth_index (gauge)
   - description: fraction of requests served with a cold prefix vs warm (0..1).
   - unit: ratio
   - SLI: track per-model and per-tenant_cohort daily

3) inference.token.hallucination_rate (counter / derived)
   - description: fraction of outputs flagged by automated QA heuristics as likely incorrect (model/applied-ml toolbox).
   - unit: percent
   - instrumentation note: derived from evaluation pipeline, not per-token expensive checks.

4) probe.query_cost_units (counter)
   - description: estimated metric for dashboard panels to show query/query-cost emitted for probes and synthetic checks.
   - unit: cost_units (internal)

Cohort logic (tenant_cohort):
- Lightweight hashing: cohort = hash(tenant_id) % 100 mapped to groups: high-volume (0-9), mid (10-39), low (40-99).
- Rationale: keep tenant_cohort limited to ~10–30 meaningful groups to reduce cardinality while preserving signal for heavy hitters.
- Owner: data infra to publish cohort mapping nightly.

Tracing / span taxonomy (proposal):
- Trace root: session_provenance_id (GUID) set at API gateway for multi-call flows. Attach as trace tag and as metric dimension where possible.
- Spans: gateway.accept, router.route_decision, model.load_weights (if long), model.infer, kv_cache.lookup, kv_cache.evict, response.serialize.
- Semantic annotations: attach model_version, quantization_profile, batching_window_ms as span attributes to aid regression hunting.
- PII policy: session_provenance_id must be an opaque token; never attach user-provided PII to spans. Use redaction hooks at SDK level.

Sampling policy (budget-aware):
- Adaptive sampling per tenant_cohort: baseline 0.5% across the board; high-volume cohorts get lower baseline (0.2%) and higher severity-triggered amplification.
- Severity amplification: if latency p99 > SLO or error rate spike detected, temporarily increase sampling for affected tenants to 100% for 10 minutes (circuit to avoid overload).
- Trace budget accounting: show real-time approximate trace cost per workspace on dashboard to avoid runaway costs.

Dashboard wireframes and investigation flow: (working bullets)
- Top row: global health (p50/p95/p99 overall), total token rate, query_cost burn rate.
- Second row: cohort selector (tenant_cohort), model filter, region filter.
- Main canvas: latency heatmap sliced by tenant_cohort vs model_version; clicking a heatmap cell triggers session_provenance_id list sample.
- Investigation panel: for selected session_provenance_id show timeline (spans), raw prompt/response artifacts (redacted), KV cache status changes, and quick links to related traces.
- Cost panel: per-cohort probe.query_cost_units and trace budget usage with color-coded warnings.

Rollout checklist (phased):
- Phase 0 (instrumentation week 1): add session_provenance_id at gateway; emit inference.request.latency_ms and token counters; add tenant_cohort dimension.
- Phase 1 (week 2–3): add span annotations, kv_cache metrics, basic dashboard with cohort selector and heatmap.
- Phase 2 (week 4): sampling policy rollout and trace budget dashboard; integrate severity amplification.
- Phase 3 (Q2): add hallucination rate pipeline hooks and long-term histogram retention changes.

Owner / stakeholders:
- Primary: eng-observability (Maya Patel)
- Instrumentation owners: serving-runtime (Lars Kim), platform-engineering (Jonas Reed)
- Product validator: Priya Menon (product-hosted-api)

Open questions / TODOs (notes to self):
- TODO: confirm cohort hashing bounds with data infra; potential privacy checks for cohort mapping.
- TODO: cost_units definition — finance needs mapping to billing. JIRA-OBS-987 assigned.
- Decide: store full trace body for 30d for high-severity tenants? privacy compliance required.
- SDK change: add redaction API (small lib) to ensure no prompt user text flows into trace attributes.

Quick instrument snippets (pseudocode):
- Http handler:
  session_provenance_id = request.header.get("X-Session-Provenance") or gen_guid()
  emit_metric("inference.request.latency_ms", duration_ms, tags={"model":m, "tenant_cohort": cohort})
  trace.set_tag("session_provenance_id", session_provenance_id)
  // ensure no user PII set on tags

Alerting heuristics (starter):
- P95 latency per-cohort > baseline_SLO * 1.5 for 15m -> PAGER if cohort in high-volume set, otherwise page-on-repeat (3x in 1h).
- probe.query_cost_units burn rate > 2x expected -> create ticket + slack alert to #ops-costs.

Appendix: references and inspiration pages
- CONFLUENCE-OBS-1234: session_provenance design doc (draft)
- GitHub PR: github.com/redwood-inference/obs-sdk/pull/42 (redaction hooks)

Notes: this doc is intentionally compact and pragmatic. Next step: sync with data infra to lock cohort mapping and retention tiers, then schedule a 30m demo with product and SREs to validate the investigation flow.

Signed-off-by: Maya Patel
